commands.name: host
commands.summary: take this machine from nothing to a running node and print its URL; bare binds loopback, --domain issues a Let's Encrypt certificate for a name you own, --public uses a magic-DNS name over this box's address, --foreground execs the daemon instead of installing a unit

commands.name: init
commands.summary: set up a node's layout on this machine: repository root, credential at 0600, an actor key the node trusts, and .choir/config; refuses to overwrite what exists

commands.name: key
commands.summary: mint a key and print the line the operator registers; pass your channel name to print the bound form

commands.name: git-credential
commands.summary: git credential helper: hands git your token on stdin so it never lives in a remote URL; configure with `git config credential.helper '!choir git-credential <auth-file>'`

commands.name: join
commands.summary: redeem an invite link and set this machine up: actor key at ~/.choir/agent.key, token at ~/.choir/auth (0600), a git credential helper for that node, and the node URL in ~/.choir/config; --user names the account when the invite left it open, asked on the terminal otherwise; the three-argument form takes the invite from a file, answers JSON and touches neither git nor your home directory

commands.name: invite
commands.summary: mint an invite and print the one link to send; the same thing the /people page does

commands.name: asks
commands.summary: who has asked for access and is waiting on an answer (D72)

commands.name: grant
commands.summary: let one of them in; the link they already hold becomes their invite

commands.name: decline
commands.summary: drop a pending request; their link then reads as never valid

commands.name: workspace
commands.summary: provision a CoW workspace; advanced flags owner-sign an exact base and stable change, and each --path owner-signs a subtree

commands.name: checkpoint
commands.summary: publish an immutable change revision after committing and pushing its git object

commands.name: propose
commands.summary: create a change, push its commits and request review, with no arguments; run from a git checkout, with the key and channel from ~/.choir, every value overridable by flag; re-running after an amend updates the same proposal; a leading `<key-file> <channel>` pair is still accepted

commands.name: workspace-archive
commands.summary: owner-sign and recoverably archive a bound workspace; exact retries are idempotent

commands.name: runner
commands.summary: drive one workspace lifecycle step for an orchestrator; JSON request on stdin, JSON result on stdout

commands.name: submit
commands.summary: sign and submit one raw operation

commands.name: schema
commands.summary: print this node's machine-readable API description and its live capabilities

commands.name: log
commands.summary: read log entries from a cursor; --verify checks continuity, recomputes every hash and verifies the signatures whose keys you hold

commands.name: batch
commands.summary: sign and submit many operations as one batch, the primary path for agent workloads; one op per line, `-` reads stdin, one result line per op

commands.name: review
commands.summary: request review on a commit; name no reviewers and the node draws them

commands.name: verdict
commands.summary: answer a review you were assigned

commands.name: comment
commands.summary: say something on a review; append-only, and the comment id is your retry identity

commands.name: viewed
commands.summary: record that you read a review; first read only, resubmitting is refused

commands.name: witness
commands.summary: cosign the node's current ref-state attestation (D67); the snapshot id is read from the view, and the node may not witness its own

commands.name: vouch
commands.summary: vouch for another operator; both ends need a key bound in the log, and it authorizes nothing on its own

commands.name: unvouch
commands.summary: withdraw a vouch; both ops stay in the log, and vouching again starts a fresh clock

commands.name: slash
commands.summary: invalidate one reviewer's approval; operator-only and never moves a ref

commands.name: abandon
commands.summary: archive a stale incomplete review as lapsed, settling it unapproved; operator-only and never moves a ref

commands.name: bind
commands.summary: record in the log that a key belongs to an operator; operator-only and never moves a ref

commands.name: revoke
commands.summary: withdraw a key binding; terminal, and the attribution row survives

commands.name: appeal
commands.summary: appeal a rejected newcomer attempt for operator adjudication; never grants privilege

commands.name: intent
commands.summary: publish a task spec or plan so other agents can see intent

commands.name: check
commands.summary: report one automated check's outcome on a commit; any runner or person can report by signing, and the node never runs the check

commands.name: checks
commands.summary: every check reported on a commit, and one verdict; exits 0 passed, 1 failed or unreported, 3 still running, 4 could not be run

commands.name: profile
commands.summary: what the log records about one actor: keys and their age, changes owned, verdicts given, checks reported

commands.name: search
commands.summary: find a literal term across every repository you may read

commands.name: reviews
commands.summary: your pending review queue

commands.name: acl render
commands.summary: rewrite an ACL file's trailing comments to name the person behind each handle; grants are copied through unchanged

commands.name: triage
commands.summary: every review and change in a bucket (landed, awaiting verdicts, changes requested, approved awaiting landing), most actionable first, capped, with truncation marked in-band

commands.name: funnel
commands.summary: the contribution funnel from admission to first verdict and the steepest drop between stages; counts what this credential may read, and reports an unmeasured stage as null

commands.name: state
commands.summary: list what you owe and what you are waiting on; every row carries the command that answers it and its risk

commands.name: docs
commands.summary: build the book from `docs/` with the API documentation inside it at `book/api/`; needs a checkout and `mdbook`, and names the install command if it is missing

commands.name: skill
commands.summary: install the choir agent skill (default .claude/skills), rendered from this binary's own surface table; re-run after upgrading

commands.name: view
commands.summary: read the materialized view, its ref-state attestation and the node's health counters; map-shaped sections page 200 rows at a time, with `<section>_omitted` and `paging.next`

commands.name: repo create
commands.summary: create a repository on a running node, sequenced from its first push; needs a node-wide write grant, answers 409 when it already exists, and prints the clone URL

commands.name: repo list
commands.summary: the repositories on a node this credential can read, one per line; an ACL narrows the list rather than refusing it

commands.name: repo url
commands.summary: the clone URL for a repository, and the one line of git configuration that makes pushing work; the credential is never put in the URL

commands.name: node serve
commands.summary: run the node in this terminal, deriving root, credential and trusted keys from what `choir init` wrote; execs the daemon so signals and the exit code reach the real process

commands.name: node install
commands.summary: hand the node to launchd (macOS) or a systemd user unit (Linux) so it survives logout, crash and reboot; the unit runs `choir node serve`

commands.name: node tls
commands.summary: obtain a Let's Encrypt certificate for this node and wire up renewal: certbot, a deploy hook that re-projects the pair and restarts the node, and the marker `node serve` reads; the only command here that expects root, and `--user` is required

commands.name: node stop
commands.summary: stop the supervised node for this boot, leaving the unit in place; `node uninstall` is the one that ends it

commands.name: node restart
commands.summary: reload the unit and start it again, which is how a rebuilt binary reaches the running node

commands.name: node uninstall
commands.summary: stop the node and remove its unit; the state directory, with the keys, repositories and op log, is kept

commands.name: node logs
commands.summary: the tail of the node's log; defaults to the last 30 lines

commands.name: node status
commands.summary: health, the commit serving, the sequencer's position and its p99 against the 100 ms gate, and how much this credential can see

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: check everything the other commands assume: the binaries shelled out to, the auth file and its mode, and whether a node answers; each failure prints the fix; on a hosting machine it adds bind address, TLS, certificate expiry, linger, unit state and whether the public URL answers

commands.name: backup verify
commands.summary: whether a backup can be restored from: the four files, the manifest checksum, the hash chain, the policy archive and every git bundle, refusing a backup that carries a key or credential; every check local

commands.name: backup restore
commands.summary: turn a backup back into a node and prove it by accepting a real push: reads and refuses before writing, unbundles git objects before the first boot, rehearses on a port it picks; exit 3 means a secret only you can supply is missing

commands.name: repair
commands.summary: inspect a stopped node's op log, or repair a tail that was still being written; `--verify` changes nothing, `--truncate-tail` quarantines the partial record before cutting, and damage anywhere but the tail is refused

deprecations.name: workspace
deprecations.note: v1 alias for the signature-covered attribution channel; accepted on submission for compatibility, and refused when it disagrees with `channel` rather than one silently winning

endpoints.name: choir_submit
endpoints.purpose: Submit one signed operation (hex payload, hex signature)

ops.description: Signed operations, admitted in array order

endpoints.name: choir_submit_batch
endpoints.purpose: Same, in array order; the primary path for agent workloads

limit.description: Rows per section; defaults to 200 and clamps to this range

offset.description: Rows skipped per section, in key order

endpoints.name: choir_view
endpoints.purpose: The materialized view plus the latest ref-state attestation, key bindings, T2 review outcomes, T3 concentration, T4 newcomer harm, view growth, the build commit, and the sequencer's p99 against the 100 ms gate. Under an ACL you get your own slice; node-wide sections need a node-wide grant, and a missing repository is one you were not granted. Map-shaped sections are bounded: `limit` rows (200 default, 1000 max), `offset`, `<section>_omitted`, and `paging.next`

attempt_id.description: Newcomer attempt id returned with the rejection

endpoints.name: choir_appeal
endpoints.purpose: Record an appeal for a rejected newcomer attempt; requests operator adjudication and never changes privilege

endpoints.name: choir_log
endpoints.purpose: Ordered log entries, the catch-up and sync primitive. Absolute `from`; evicted entries are served from the persisted log (`source` says which), and a node that cannot reach back answers 409. Each entry carries hash, parent and author signature; SYNC.md is the verification procedure

This node's public key and every key it trusts, with the channel a key is bound to, versioned: what SYNC.md's authorship check needs, since the log names a key's id and never the key. Behind the same node-wide read grant as `/api/log`

base.description: Exact full Git commit oid; advanced requests provide this with owner, change and idempotency_key

owner.description: Registered signing channel allowed to checkpoint and archive the stable change

payload_hex.description: Hex-encoded CreateAuthorization for the exact binding

signature_hex.description: Owner signature over the create authorization

endpoints.name: choir_workspace
endpoints.purpose: Provision a CoW workspace; optional exact base/change binding makes retries idempotent

change.description: Stable logical change id returned by creation

channel.description: Bound change owner and signature-covered attribution channel

payload_hex.description: Hex-encoded ArchiveAuthorization naming this exact change, workspace and revision

endpoints.name: choir_workspace_archive
endpoints.purpose: Recoverably archive a change-bound workspace and remove it from the active view

limit.description: Rows per section; defaults to 200 and clamps to this range

offset.description: Rows skipped per section, in key order

endpoints.name: choir_reviews
endpoints.purpose: One actor's pending review queue

endpoints.name: choir_schema
endpoints.purpose: This surface, machine-readable and versioned, plus what this node will accept; the description an agent generates a client from (D17)

in.description: What to look through; defaults to code

limit.description: Matches returned; defaults to 200. `matches` counts everything found either way

q.description: Literal term, not a pattern; matching is case-insensitive

repo.description: One repository as owner/name; omit to search every repository you may read

rev.description: Revision to search, for a single repo= only; defaults to HEAD

endpoints.name: choir_search
endpoints.purpose: Search repository contents, file names or commit messages across every repository you may read, each at HEAD; `rev` needs a single `repo`. Ungranted repositories are absent, or answered as nonexistent by name. Unindexed (`git grep`): `limit` bounds the results, `matches` counts everything, `truncated` says which

channel.description: The name an actor signs as

endpoints.name: choir_profile
endpoints.purpose: One actor's standing out of the view you may see: bound keys and their age, changes owned, reviews assigned and verdicts given, approvals slashed, checks reported, and `vouches` with direction. Two callers with different grants get different numbers. No score; time-locked grants (D66) live outside the log and are not counted
This surface, as text, for an agent that has never seen choir
The sync contract: cursor semantics and how to verify a page's hash chain and author signatures
Which repositories this credential can see, read from the filesystem; `narrowed` says whether an ACL was applied
Create a repository on a running node with the `pre-receive` hook that sequences its pushes; needs a node-wide write grant; appends nothing to the log
Where the op log and the bare repos disagree about a ref, read-only
Mint a single-use, expiring invite and the grants it will hold; needs a node-wide write grant and can never issue one; a grant may carry `until=<unix seconds>` (D66)
Redeem an invite, presented as the credential, for a token, once, and register an ssh key
Answer an access request (D72): turns it into an invite under the id and secret the asker already holds
Drop a pending access request; their link then reads as never valid
Delete an account: its token stops authenticating on the next request, and its grants and keys go with it
Who holds an account, what they were granted, and which invites are outstanding; never a secret or its hash
Internal: the pre-receive hook callback
Internal: retracts a refused push's already-accepted refs
